title: Revenge trading and tilt
desc: Stop one bad trade from turning into a bad day

cards.title: After a bad morning
cards.situation: You lost $300 on your first trade today. You’re angry. A so-so setup appears, and you want to double your size to win it back. What should you do?

visual.title: Today’s P&L
visual.label: Today’s profit and loss falls to −$300

options.text: Double up: one good trade fixes it
options.feedback: Most people feel that urge. Bigger size on a weak setup turns one bad trade into a bad week.

options.text: Take it at your normal size
options.feedback: Better than doubling, but anger is still choosing the trade. A so-so setup on a hot head is how one loss becomes two.

options.text: Skip it and step away for today
options.feedback: Anger makes bad setups look good. Stepping away keeps one loss from turning into three.

cards.work: Down $300. Double size on a weak setup: one more loss costs $600, and the day ends at −$900.

cards.title: Revenge trading and tilt
cards.text: **[[revenge-trading|Revenge trading]]** is rushing into a bigger trade to win back a loss. **[[tilt|Tilt]]** is the angry state behind it. Poker players named it.

visual.caption: Your trade size, loss after loss

blocks.tip: Signs of tilt: bigger size, faster trades, setups you’d normally skip, and a hot head.

cards.title: How a bad day snowballs
cards.text: Say you lose $100 twice, then double your size each time to win it back.

items.title: Rule: stop after 2 losses
items.label: With the rule: two $100 losses, then no more trades, ending at −$200

blocks.tip: Same losses, same day. The rule kept the loss at $200 instead of $800.

cards.title: Decide the limit before the day starts
cards.text: Write your limits **before** the first trade, while you’re calm. Then you don’t have to decide anything when you’re angry.

items.title: 2 losses in a day: done
items.text: Close the app. Tomorrow is a new day.

items.title: A daily loss limit
items.text: For example 2% of the account: $200 on $10,000.

items.title: Never size up to win it back
items.text: Same size after a loss, or smaller.

cards.title: Rule or setup?
cards.q: Your rule: stop after 2 losses a day. It’s 11am and you’ve lost on trades 1 and 2. Then a perfect setup appears. What do you do?

options.text: Take it: it’s a perfect setup
options.feedback: Most people feel that pull. A rule only works if it holds on the days it hurts. Setups come back tomorrow, a blown account doesn’t.

options.text: Stop for the day, as your rule says
options.feedback: The rule holds on the day it hurts. Setups come back tomorrow, and your account will be there for them.
Smaller size still breaks the rule. The rule is about you after two losses, not about this setup.
Doubling after two losses is revenge trading. Your rule exists for exactly this moment.

cards.title: Spot the tilt
cards.q: Which of these is a sign you’re on tilt?

options.text: Keeping your normal size after a loss
options.feedback: Easy to mix up: normal size after a loss is discipline. Sizing up to win it back is tilt.

options.text: Raising your size to win a loss back
options.feedback: Bigger size to win it back is the classic sign: anger is choosing the trade.

options.text: Taking a break after a loss
options.feedback: A break after a loss is the cure for tilt, not a sign of it.

options.text: Writing the loss in your journal
options.feedback: Logging a loss is a calm, healthy habit. Tilt shows up as bigger size and faster trades.

cards.headline: You can stop a bad day from getting worse.
lines: Revenge trading = a bigger trade to win back a loss.
Set a daily limit, like stop after 2 losses.
Never size up after a loss.
